notes:
**A defence that every page has no longer counts as a defence.**

The AI-substitution section reports which of your pages an assistant can
replace and which have a reason to be visited. On a 60-page shop it reported
all sixty as defended, at a risk of exactly zero — because a basket link, a
newsletter box and a log-in link appear on every page. Sixty pages, one value,
presented as a portfolio. A signal every page carries cannot tell you which
pages are defended, so those are now excluded, and the report says which ones
it excluded and why.

**One form no longer counts as two defences.**

A form was read both as "the visitor can act here" and as "something to
operate", so a newsletter box took twice the credit off a page's exposure.
Measured on a blog-heavy SaaS site, the form in question sat on 94 of 200
pages — the blog template, not the product pages. A subscribe box is not a
calculator; it is now counted once, as what it is.

**"Defended" now says what share of your pages the defence covers.**

A count on its own reads as a verdict. On the same site, 141 of 200 pages came
back defended, and the defence carrying most of them was on 75% of everything
assessed. That number is now printed next to the count, so you can see whether
a verdict rests on something specific to those pages or on something the whole
site has.
